gold.summary: Unlimited quota still applies utilization reserves to free and metered providers.

findings.title: Unlimited only bypasses windows for subscription billing
findings.detail: `headroom()` drops windows only when `billing === "subscription" && quota === "unlimited"`. The request says an unlimited provider "always has headroom 1, and reserves don't gate it". If a provider is configured with metered or free billing plus `quota = "unlimited"` and its harness reports windows (any claude-harness provider can emit rate_limit events), those windows still gate it. The setting is then silently ignored.
findings.failure_scenario: `[[providers]] id="x" kind="anthropic-compatible" billing="metered" quota="unlimited"` observes `five_hour` at 1.0; `headroom("x")` returns 0 and the provider is reported as "at reserve limit".

findings.title: Existing window alerts are never cleared after switching to unlimited
findings.detail: `observeWindows` now returns before the alert-clearing loop for unlimited providers. A warning or exhausted alert recorded while the provider was in "windows" mode stays visible after the user switches to unlimited, until its `resetsAt` passes. If `resetsAt` is null and `listAlerts` keeps such alerts, it stays indefinitely. That contradicts "quota alerts don't fire for an unlimited provider's windows".
findings.failure_scenario: Claude has a five_hour warning alert at 80%. The user sets `quota = "unlimited"` and restarts. New observations never clear the alert, so the UI keeps showing a quota warning.

findings.title: Export now writes `quota = "windows"` for every provider
findings.detail: Because of `quota.default("windows")` in providerSchema and the normalisation in resolveCatalog, `limitless providers export` adds `quota = "windows"` to every exported provider. This churns users' config files with a default value.
findings.failure_scenario: Running `limitless providers export --write` on an existing config adds a `quota = "windows"` line to every provider block.

findings.failure_scenario: Pin verify to ["claude/opus", "codex/sol"]. Opus returns only environment-blocked criteria; the reserved retry runs opus again. If opus remains blocked, the run needs a human without ever attempting sol.

findings.title: Keep exhausted implementers excluded after escalation
findings.detail: triedImplementers is applied only on the escalation round. Subsequent rounds pass only the current implementer preference, allowing routing back to an exhausted earlier candidate if the current model becomes unavailable. Read-only reproduction of those subsequent-round constraints: `bun -e 'import {Router} from "./src/router/router.ts"; import {MODELS,PROVIDERS} from "./src/router/catalog.ts"; const r=new Router({def:id=>PROVIDERS.find(p=>p.id===id),headroom:()=>1,unavailableReason:id=>id==="codex"?"disabled":null,modelUnavailableReason:()=>null}, {}, MODELS); console.log(r.route("implement","small",{chain:["claude/opus","codex/sol"],prefer:"codex/sol"},false).candidates.map(m=>m.modelId));'
findings.failure_scenario: Opus uses its two rounds and escalates to sol. Sol completes one unsuccessful round, then its provider is disabled or becomes quota-exhausted. The next round invokes opus again instead of stopping with needs_human because the chain is exhausted.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: A classifier exception for one PR stops observation of every later PR in the repository
findings.detail: classifyCi throws on many conditions: an HTTP response other than 200 on any REST read ('Incomplete CI inspection'), zod parse failures, 'Outdated CI check completion', 'Ambiguous CI rerun job', 'Incomplete failing check', and a rerun response other than 201. Nothing catches the error inside record(), so it escapes the `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries())` loop in observe(). tick() catches it per repository and logs it. Every PR after the failing one in that batch is then never recorded, so it gets no pr.ci_failed, pr.merged, pr.closed or review items and no snapshot update. The setGithubAccess completion bookkeeping is skipped as well. ciPending is saved as true before classification, so
findings.failure_scenario: Repo o/r tracks PR #1 and PR #2. PR #1 has a failed Actions job whose log download keeps returning 410 or 403 (expired retention, or a token without Actions read). On every poll, read() throws 'Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/N/logs (410)'. PR #2 is merged on GitHub, but its github_prs data n

findings.title: Matrix siblings cancelled by fail-fast are rerun and recorded as flakes
findings.detail: `transient` is true for any check or job whose conclusion is 'cancelled'. The only supersession check is that the remote PR head still equals the snapshot head. GitHub Actions cancels the remaining matrix jobs when one fails (fail-fast is the default), and those cancellations happen at the same SHA. Each cancelled sibling has its own check name, so each gets its own signature and its own rerun. When a rerun passes, the row is marked 'failed_then_passed', which the request defines as the only evidence of nondeterminism. A job that was cancelled and then ran to success is not nondeterministic, so the ledger now holds false flake evidence. The request limits cancelled reruns to runs cancelled '
findings.failure_scenario: A workflow has the matrix test [ubuntu, macos, windows]. test (ubuntu) fails a real assertion, and GitHub cancels test (macos) and test (windows). The classifier emits ci.needs_fix for ubuntu, POSTs reruns for macos and windows, and when they pass, writes two 'failed_then_passed' flake rows for chec

findings.title: The rerun cap is spent when GitHub rejects a job rerun while its workflow run is still in progress
findings.detail: The rollup turns FAILURE as soon as any check fails, even while other jobs in the same workflow run are still running. The classifier then claims the cap (claimCiRerun sets rerun_claimed=1 and outcome=rerun_requested) and POSTs actions/jobs/{id}/rerun. I believe GitHub only re-runs a job once its whole workflow run has completed and rejects the request before then; I could not confirm this against the live API. The code then throws 'CI job rerun was not confirmed'. On the next poll, the row is found with outcome 'rerun_requested', marked 'failed_again', and reported as ci.needs_fix. The timed-out job is never rerun, so the main acceptance criterion fails for any workflow with more than one j
findings.failure_scenario: A workflow has jobs `smoke` (timeout 5 min) and `e2e` (30 min). `smoke` times out at minute 5. The rollup is FAILURE, the poller classifies it as transient, claims the cap and POSTs the rerun; if GitHub rejects it because `e2e` is still running, the next poll emits ci.needs_fix and the transient fai

findings.title: About twice the requested change budget, with heavy defensive complexity
findings.detail: The request set a budget of about 250 changed source lines. The diff adds about 490 (357 in ci-classifier.ts alone) plus two migrations for one new table. classifyCi is a single 300-line function with many nested throw/continue/return paths and two different 'current' and 'ready' callbacks. That makes properties like 'at most one rerun per PR, SHA and signature' hard to verify by reading, and it contributes to the throw-propagation problem above.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure. It is a maintainability and scope cost against the stated budget.

findings.title: A second migration alters a table added in the same change
findings.detail: 20261005T0737-ci-failures.sql creates ci_failures, and a second migration in the same unreleased change adds rerun_job to it. That is needless churn for an additive migration that has not been released.
findings.failure_scenario: None at runtime.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: A rejected rerun request leaves classification pending forever
findings.detail: The claim persists rerun_requested before the POST, but an explicit rejection never resolves that claim. Subsequent polls wait for run_attempt to increase and suppress ci.needs_fix indefinitely. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501/ci-review-rejection.ts. Output: Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed; subsequent polls returned {"done":false,"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job qualifies for retry, but GitHub returns HTTP 422 or a permission rejection. No new attempt starts, so the PR remains pending permanently.

findings.title: Main-red failures never enter the flake ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching failure evidence or recording a CiFailure. Consequently, non-security failures suppressed because main is red have no ledger signature, SHA, runner image, or outcome, contrary to the requirement to record each failure signature. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501/ci-review-main-red.ts. Output on every poll: {"done":false,"posts":0,"ledgerRows":0,"mainRed":true}.
findings.failure_scenario: Both the factory PR and main fail the test check. The classifier emits ci.main_red, but the failure is never recorded if the PR closes or receives another SHA before main recovers.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Daemon fails to boot when a runtime model collides with a later config model or its provider is removed
findings.detail: Factory's constructor reloads stored runtime models with `throw new Error('catalog collision: …')` and `throw new Error('unknown provider …')`. A routine operator workflow breaks startup: try a model at runtime, then promote it into config.toml's `[[providers.models]]` under the same id, or remove a config-defined provider. The Factory constructor throws and the daemon will not start. The only fix then is editing SQLite by hand, and the API can't help because the server is down. Nothing at the config-loading stage warns about this.
findings.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a scratch test (rvtest/boot.test.ts in a TMPDIR copy). `factory.catalog.add({...customModel, provider:'mac-mlx'})`, then restart with config.toml defining mac-mlx/flash: `Error: catalog collision: mac-mlx/flash`. Restart with mac-mlx removed from config: `Error: unknown provid

findings.title: DELETE checks only operator cells; a policy.json reference then breaks the next startup
findings.detail: `remove()` checks only `store.routingCells()`. Because runtime models are merged before `readPolicy`, the policy.json overlay at policyPath can validly name a runtime model. Deleting that model succeeds. On the next restart, `readPolicy` validates against a catalog that no longer has the model, throws 'Invalid routing policy', and the daemon fails to start.
findings.failure_scenario: Scratch test: add codex/experiment, write policy.json `{triage:{default:['codex/experiment@high','claude/opus']}}`, then build a Factory with that policyPath. `catalog.remove('codex/experiment')` is allowed, and building a new Factory then throws `Invalid routing policy …/policy.json`.

findings.title: Smoke silently drops checks for disabled or missing providers
findings.detail: Before this change, smoke threw if claude, codex, omlx, twilight, openrouter or typesafe was missing. Now it filters out providers with a runtime enabled override of false and uses `continue` / `return checks` when a provider is absent. So a provider that is disabled at runtime, or missing from config, simply disappears from the deploy gate with no skip line. That is a behaviour change outside the request. Smoke also now opens the live SQLite DB, running migrations, to read overrides.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator disables `claude` on the Providers page and deploys. Smoke prints no claude checks at all instead of reporting them as skipped, and the deploy gate passes without exercising claude.

findings.title: Test client decodes the :id param itself, so it doesn't verify decoding of the encoded slash
findings.detail: Model ids contain '/', so the CLI and docs send `codex%2Fexperiment`. The test helper calls `decodeURIComponent(parts[4])` itself, so the tests never check that Bun's real router matches and decodes `%2F` into `req.params.id`. I could not check this because the sandbox blocks listening sockets.
findings.failure_scenario: If Bun passes the raw `codex%2Fexperiment`, the server-side lookup fails with 'missing catalog model', and `limitless catalog remove` and PATCH stop working.

gold.summary: Effort removal is persisted without checking policy cells hidden by operator overrides.

findings.title: Deletion can leave the eval policy invalid and prevent restart
findings.detail: remove() checks only persisted operator cells. A runtime model can also be referenced by routing/policy.json, including through the existing eval-policy workflow. Deletion succeeds while leaving that policy unchanged. Factory startup subsequently calls readPolicy(), which rejects the missing model and aborts construction. Reproduced with this exact command: bun -e 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { MODELS, PROVIDERS, DEFAULT_POLICY } from "./src/router/catalog.ts"; import { ProviderTracker } from "./src/router/providers.ts"; import { Router } from "./src/router/router.ts"; import { RuntimeCatalog } from "./src/router/runtime-catalog.ts"; import { parsePolicy, overlayPolicy
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment, persist an eval policy naming it, restart to activate that policy, then remove the model without an operator-cell reference. DELETE succeeds, but the next daemon restart fails while validating routing/policy.json.

gold.summary: Digest actions are derived from stale records instead of current unanswered and review state.
A historical failed review hides a later approval in MCP status.

findings.title: Blocked-land items are never cleared by PR merge/close
findings.detail: The 'Blocked lands' group clears only on land.queued and land.landed. land.blocked items are keyed by data.url (the PR URL). pr.merged and pr.closed items carry that same url key, as does run.merged with data.prUrl, but none of these kinds is in that group's clears list.
findings.failure_scenario: A land is blocked, and an operator then merges or closes the PR manually on GitHub. The poller emits pr.merged with data.url equal to the PR URL. Every later `limitless digest` still reports 'Blocked lands: 1' for a PR that has already merged, until the consumer acks past it.

findings.title: Answered questions stay under 'Needs you' until the run reaches a terminal state
findings.detail: run.question is cleared only by terminal run events. Answering a question emits no feed item, and the run's return to running emits none either, so an answered question keeps counting as needing attention.
findings.failure_scenario: A run asks a question, and the user answers it in the dashboard. The run then stays running for hours. The SessionStart digest keeps showing that run under 'Needs you' with the question title, which sends agents to answer a question that is already answered.

findings.title: MCP verdicts are recorded as reviewer "human"
findings.detail: The limitless_review tool drops `reviewer`, so `submitReview` records `parsed.data.reviewer ?? "human"`. Other MCP mutations attribute their source (answer sends by: "mcp"). Approvals made by an agent through MCP are therefore indistinguishable from human approvals in the review_approvals table and in the review.approved feed summary.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent calls limitless_review with verdict approve. The feed shows 'approved at <sha> by human', so the audit trail misattributes the approval.

gold.summary: Embedded short registered secrets remain visible in digest fields.
MCP status returns private land reasons unchanged on direct and proxy backends.

findings.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema discards run.merged, and explainStatus never checks it. Existing automatic delivery and GitHub reconciliation can set merged=true without a merged PR snapshot, resolution, or land entry. The tool then tells an agent to review or land an already merged PR. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {explainStatus,statusDetailSchema} from "./src/integrations/mcp-status.ts"; const detail = statusDetailSchema.parse({run:{id:"merged-run",status:"succeeded",prUrl:"https://github.com/o/r/pull/1",merged:true},questions:[],prSnapshot:{state:"OPEN",headRefOid:"a".repeat(40)},review:{approval:null,rounds:[]}}); console.log(JSON.stringify(explainStatus(detail,[])));' Output: {"run":"merged-run",
findings.failure_scenario: An automatically merged succeeded run has merged=true, no land entry, and an absent or previously OPEN saved PR observation. limitless_status incorrectly requests further review instead of reporting Landed.

gold.summary: Layered URL and Unicode encodings bypass the single-pass private-text decoder.

findings.title: Digest lists PRs as awaiting review while their run is still in progress
findings.detail: The 'PRs awaiting review' filter checks only that the run is not resolved, cancelled or merged, that a PR exists, that the PR is not closed, and the approval and land state. It does not require the run to be finished. submitReview refuses any owner whose status is not succeeded or needs_human. So a run that opened its PR and is still running (CI wait, verify) shows up as review-ready, and a review verdict would be refused with 409. explainStatus handles this case as 'Work pending', so the two tools disagree.
findings.failure_scenario: A run emits run.pr_opened, then sits in status 'running' waiting on CI. The digest shows 'PRs awaiting review: 1', but limitless_review returns 'only a finished run ... can be reviewed'.

findings.title: Publication-gate decoding changed outside the requested scope
findings.detail: privateMatches now also decodes literal \uXXXX escapes. That function is the shared publication gate used by the engine, not only the new output privacy. The change alters gate behaviour for all runs, which may block content that previously passed. Combined with the new private-output layer applied to every existing MCP tool, the diff goes well beyond the ~200-line budget and the stated feature.
findings.failure_scenario: A diff containing a JSON-escaped form of a private string (e.g. acme) is now blocked by the publication gate, where it was previously allowed.

findings.title: GET /api/land?run=<unknown> returns 400 rather than 404
findings.detail: LandQueue.list(runId) throws a plain Error('run not found'). The HTTP handle wrapper maps any thrown error to 400, so an unknown run is reported as a bad request instead of not found.
findings.failure_scenario: curl '/api/land?run=nope' returns HTTP 400 {error:'run not found'}.

gold.summary: Digest title truncation occurs before filtering and discloses private prefixes.

findings.title: Unread PR updates can hide a newly stale approval
findings.detail: Review candidates are collected only from PR-opened, round-delivered and approved events. An unread pr.ci_passed event on a changed head therefore never reaches current-state reconciliation, even when the approval is stale. Reproduction command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-digest.test.ts". The stale-approval test failed with Expected: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0"; Received: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0".
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer acknowledges the original PR and approval events. Someone pushes another commit; the poller marks the approval stale and emits pr.ci_passed. The next session digest reports no review work.

findings.title: Active correction rounds are counted as awaiting review
findings.detail: The review predicate ignores review.rounds. A PR whose requested changes are still running is presented as awaiting another review. Reproduction command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-digest.test.ts". The active-round test failed with Expected: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0"; Received: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0".
findings.failure_scenario: The original PR-opened event remains unread, a changes verdict starts round1, and round1 is running. The session digest asks for review before the correction round delivers.

gold.summary: Post-check publication scanning executes Git against mutable clone configuration.

findings.title: Clean-filter tests never hit the key-enumeration race from #402
findings.detail: Both clean-filter scenarios plant filter.attack.clean before safe_git's `git config --name-only --get-regexp` read: one during `bun run check`, the other in the fake `gh pr view`. A clone-level safe_git call would therefore always neutralise the filter through --config-env, so the marker could never run even if the dirty check went back to the clone's config. In my mutation run, a clone-level `safe_git status --porcelain` passed the marker assertion in these tests; they failed only on the argv assertions for the status call.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutate land-pr.sh to run `safe_git status --porcelain` against the clone before the isolated check. checks:clean-filter and pre-push:clean-filter still pass `expect(existsSync(marker)).toBe(false)` and fail only because the status argv check expects --untracked-files=normal.

findings.title: An in-progress rebase is not refused
findings.detail: The state check covers MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD and REVERT_HEAD (exactly the request) but not rebase-merge/ or rebase-apply/. A half-finished rebase with a clean tree would land its detached HEAD. The pinned-SHA comparison still guarantees that what's pushed is what was checked.
findings.failure_scenario: The orchestrator leaves a rebase stopped mid-way with a clean tree; land-pr pushes the partially rebased HEAD.

gold.summary: Forced-color Bun result markers are not recognized by failure extraction.

findings.title: Bun's end-of-run failed-test list is extracted again as extra 'failures', and can wrongly add the 'left out' note
findings.detail: The issue says that at the end of a long run bun prints the skipped list and then the failed test names as `(fail) name` lines. `FailureExcerpts.observe` treats every `(fail)` line as a new failure. So each summary line becomes another excerpt: the first one is "N tests failed:\n(fail) t0", the rest are bare duplicates. They use failure slots and character budget, and they can set `omitted` even when every real failure was kept.
findings.failure_scenario: Output with 10 real failure blocks followed by bun's "10 tests failed:" list of the same 10 `(fail)` lines. The excerpt keeps the 10 real blocks, then the summary lines hit the 10-failure cap and add the "left out" note although nothing was left out. With 3 failures the result ends in "3 tests faile

findings.title: Land log now keeps only a 1,000-char tail when excerpts exist (was the full 6,000-char tail)
findings.detail: `formatGateOutput(r, 9_000)` always uses `result.output.slice(-1_000)` as the tail. So a failed land check's log loses about 5,000 characters it used to contain, such as other stderr messages or output from non-test steps. The request asks for a shorter tail only in `formatGateFeedback`. For the land log it only asks that excerpts come before the tail. The UI panel (`ArtifactsPanel.tsx`) has the same cut, which was not requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A land check fails a test and also prints a relevant error 2,000 characters before the end of its output (for example a teardown or unhandled-rejection message). That message used to appear in land-<id>.log and now does not.

gold.summary: Unavailable-target diagnostics expose registered credentials in routing API and Setup output.

findings.title: `limitless local` crashes when remote_host includes a port or is an IPv6 address
findings.detail: manageLocal builds `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` without catching errors, before any SSH call. Some values that SSH accepts as a host make this throw a TypeError, so `limitless local up|down|status` exits with an error and doesn't even report oMLX. The old code only passed the URL to the probe, which handled the failure.
findings.failure_scenario: With `[local] remote_host = "gpu-box:2222"` or `"fe80::1"`, `manageLocal('status', …)` throws `TypeError: Invalid URL` (I reproduced this with a small script).

findings.title: A provider reached through an SSH tunnel is never matched, so its health probe is sent without the API key
findings.detail: The remote provider is found only when its `openaiBaseUrl` has the same origin as `http://<remote_host>:8080`. If the LAN provider is reached through `ssh_forward` (base URL on 127.0.0.1:18080), nothing matches. `status`/`up` then probe `http://<host>:8080/v1/models` without a token and won't enable or disable the provider. The docs mention this limit only briefly.
findings.failure_scenario: The provider is configured with ssh_forward {host = remote_host, local_port = 18080} and the server requires an API key. `local up` reports the endpoint as unreachable and never re-enables the provider.

gold.summary: Retired identifiers and catalog or routing history can publish registered credentials.

findings.title: Validate retired references that become live after a catalog addition
findings.detail: The affected-reference filter checks only the old catalog, so adding back an absent model never validates saved references to that ID. A persisted operator reference with an effort unsupported by the restored model is accepted during the addition, but RuntimePolicy rejects it on the next daemon startup. Direct reproduction command: bun -e 'import {RuntimeCatalog} from "./src/router/runtime-catalog.ts"; import {MODELS,PROVIDERS} from "./src/router/catalog.ts"; import {validatePolicy} from "./src/router/policy.ts"; const models=[...MODELS]; const policy={triage:{default:["codex/restored@high"]}}; const store={listRuns:()=>[],writeRuntimeModel:()=>{},publishCatalog:()=>{},catalogHistory:()=>[]}
findings.failure_scenario: Persist triage.default=["codex/restored@high"], start with that model absent, then add codex/restored supporting only "none". The addition succeeds and persists the model; restarting the daemon fails while validating the saved operator cell.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.
Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Truncated ANSI sequences defeat the credential overlap removal
findings.detail: When the raw runner tail starts inside an ANSI sequence embedded in a credential, stripVTControlCharacters leaves the incomplete sequence's printable suffix. Removing secret.length - 1 normalized characters then removes that formatting suffix plus only part of the credential fragment. The remaining credential suffix reaches gate storage and model feedback. Exact reproduction: bun -e 'import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {redactGateStreams} from "./src/gates/output.ts"; const secret="synthetic-truecolor-boundary-credential-421"; registerCredential("TRUECOLOR_REVIEW_TOKEN",secret); const prefix="[38;2;255;255;255m"+secret.slice(1); const room=64000-prefix.length; const
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential is printed with a true-color escape after its first character, followed by enough terminal formatting to exceed the 64,000-character runner cap. The cut removes the first credential character and the escape introducer, leaving printable escape parameters ahead of the credenti

gold.summary: Redacting the carry early emits suffixes of overlapping registered credentials.
ANSI stripping after framing and tail cuts leaves accidental credential fragments visible.

findings.title: Privacy filter now withholds any text containing "[redacted]" in full
findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string containing the literal "[redacted]". This filter runs on every MCP tool result (`privateOutputData`), on digest output and on `explainStatus`. Now that gate output (and the redaction marker in it) flows into run state, feed text and reasons, a single redacted credential hides the whole field from operators, not just the secret. The same happens to any user or agent text that simply contains the word "[redacted]". The request didn't ask for this, and redaction already removes the value itself.
findings.failure_scenario: Ran `loadOutputPrivacy()("Run blocked: lint failed. Output: token=[redacted] in fixture; please fix the test")` and got "[withheld: private text]". Any MCP status, feed or digest field quoting redacted gate output becomes unreadable.

findings.title: Every HTTP/SSE response goes through gate-data redaction, which rewrites unrelated objects
findings.detail: `json()` and the SSE `send` now pass every payload through `redactGateData`. That costs a JSON round-trip per response, strips VT control characters from every string, and adds a `confinementError` field to any object that has `ok` and `output` fields, whether or not it is a gate result. The artifact endpoint also re-parses JSON artifacts and re-serializes them compactly, so it no longer serves the stored bytes. The prompt and report paths (`implementPrompt`, `reviewPrompt`, `renderReport`, `RunContext` constructor) do the same thing to whole input objects. Together this pushes the change to about 300 source lines against a stated budget of about 30, and the request explicitly asked for reda
findings.failure_scenario: `redactGateData({status:{ok:true,output:'x'}})` returns `{status:{ok:true,output:'x',confinementError:false}}`. Any API object with that shape gets an extra field, and a pretty-printed JSON artifact is served compacted.

gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.
Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Restrict gate-specific object rewriting to gate results
findings.detail: The helper identifies gate results solely by `ok` and `output`, but HTTP serialization now applies it to every response and artifact. Consequently, unrelated application data acquires a fabricated confinement verdict. Running `bun -e 'import {redactGateData} from "./src/gates/output.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(redactGateData({ok:true,output:"ordinary application result"})));'` produces `{"ok":true,"output":"ordinary application result","confinementError":false}`. This changes unrelated artifact content and exceeds the requested gate-output scope.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-gate JSON artifact contains `{ "ok": true, "output": "ordinary application result" }`. Downloading it through the artifact endpoint adds `confinementError: false`, although the stored artifact contains no such field.

gold.summary: Nesting Seatbelt around internally sandboxed CLIs prevents tool-enabled invocations from starting.
Scanning ordinary agent output for sandbox diagnostics can discard successful invocations.
Ordinary gate output mentioning sandbox failures can turn a successful check into a confinement error.
The live confinement smoke accepts refusal even when enforcement should work.

findings.title: Detect signals executed inside shell expansions
findings.detail: Double-quoted arguments are treated as opaque strings, and non-interpreter heredocs are discarded entirely. Both can execute command substitutions, so real kill attempts disappear from warnings, the feed, and reports. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\""), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent submits echo "$(kill -TERM 123)" or an unquoted cat heredoc containing $(kill -TERM 123). The shell attempts the signal, but neither harness emits a warning.

findings.title: Preserve executable JavaScript template interpolations
findings.detail: jsSignal removes entire template literals, including executable ${...} expressions. A process.kill call inside an interpolation is therefore missed in both shell-invoked JavaScript and JavaScript tools. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("node -e '\''console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'\''"), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent runs node -e 'console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'. JavaScript attempts the signal, but the event log and report contain no signal warning.

gold.summary: LFS exemptions permit missing payloads and pointer replacements containing archives.
The limited text sample exempts a TAR whose first binary byte lies beyond the sample.
The WebP inspector rejects valid lossy VP8 images.

findings.title: Restore every explicitly permitted media extension
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH omits bmp, avif, tif/tiff, heic, psd, mp4, m4a, mkv, mov, avi, webm, aac, eot, pdf, glb, fbx and blend. These now require Allow: binary, contrary to the requested list and explicit MP4/PDF acceptance checks. The new parser also lacks these formats, so changing the regex alone is insufficient. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501/review-inert-media.ts`. Both additions and edits output included `binary-content/block: document.pdf`, using the supplied complete PDF fixtures. The new tests incorrectly assert that PDFs must block.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a binary PDF or MP4 without Allow: binary; the audit blocks the requested inert-media exemption.

findings.title: Preserve exemptions for valid media containing ordinary metadata
findings.detail: The new validator rejects standard PNG tEXt chunks, including harmless author metadata, because they are absent from its fixed chunk whitelist. Similar restrictions reject JPEG EXIF/comments and MP3 ID3 tags. This adds content restrictions absent from the request and blocks ordinary files in explicitly permitted formats. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501/review-inert-media.ts`. Both additions and edits output included `binary-content/block: author.png`; the otherwise identical PNG without the valid Author tEXt chunk passed.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PNG containing a CRC-correct `Author\0Matt` tEXt chunk; the audit requires Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not remove media exemptions above 32 MiB
findings.detail: Any media blob larger than MEDIA_LIMIT is skipped and consequently included in binaryPaths, regardless of whether it is valid inert media. The request has no size-dependent allowance requirement. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-LzstG3/claude-501/review-inert-media.ts`. Both additions and edits output included `binary-content/block: silence.wav` for a valid mono PCM WAV with 32 MiB of samples plus its 44-byte header.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid WAV larger than 32 MiB without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it solely because of its size.

gold.summary: Detached descendants survive invocation cleanup and keep modifying the worktree.
Process cleanup returns while owned descendants are still alive.
Discarding changes replaces the cleanup error that should trigger round recovery.

findings.title: Final cleanup can mask the recoverable cleanup error
findings.detail: The gates callback always calls discardChanges in its finally block. When the two -ffdxq attempts leave an untracked, non-ignored directory that cannot be removed, discardChanges runs clean -fdq and throws CommandError. That replaces WorktreeCleanError, so this new handler rethrows and fails the run. Reproduced with the actual checkoutCommitted and discardChanges functions and a temporary Git shim that reports an untracked blocked directory and fails clean. Output: {"caught":"CommandError","roundFailureHandlerMatches":false,"message":"Command failed (1): git clean -fdq\nwarning: failed to remove blocked/file: Permission denied"}.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer leaves a non-ignored directory whose contents cannot be removed. Both clean retries fail, then discardChanges fails on the same directory and bypasses round recovery.

findings.title: Process-group termination does not kill the whole descendant tree
findings.detail: The new exit handler still signals only the invocation's original process group. A descendant spawned with detached:true has another process group and survives. This is a pre-existing limitation left unresolved by the requested fix. Exact check: bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const program = `const {spawn}=require("node:child_process"); const p=spawn(process.execPath,["-e","setInterval(()=>{},1000)"],{detached:true,stdio:"ignore"}); console.log(p.pid); p.unref();`; let pid; try { const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",program],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env}); pid=Number(r.stdout.trim()); console.log(JSON.stringify({exitCode:r.exitCode,descendantPid:p
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached background writer with redirected stdio and then exits or is stopped. runProcess returns while the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

gold.summary: Shutdown drops an already claimed descendant when its parent exits.
Holdout snapshot deletion proceeds despite unconfirmed descendant termination.
Production scratch directories are never registered as process ownership roots.
Replacing a descendant environment removes it from invocation discovery.

findings.title: Process discovery misses owned children with replacement environments
findings.detail: Session/group membership is accepted only when the environment is hidden. A regular executable launched with a replacement environment containing PATH but no invocation marker is excluded, even when it remains in the invocation's process group. Removing the previous group kill therefore introduces a regression: runProcess reports confirmed shutdown while the child keeps writing. The standalone same-group assertion failed with `Expected: 4; Received: 29` bytes after return; against the base implementation it passed with `sameGroupBytesAtReturn: 1, sameGroupBytesAfterReturn: 1`. The detached-shell case also failed (`Expected: 1278; Received: 9508`) when the shell changed cwd to / and wrote thr
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a background test runner with an explicitly constructed environment, then exits or is stopped. The runner remains alive after runProcess returns and races with worktree cleanup.

findings.title: Cwd and birth time do not establish ownership of an orphan
findings.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden-environment process born after invocation start whose cwd is within a captured directory, without proving ancestry or marker ownership. An unrelated launcher can create exactly that state. The standalone native-inspection assertion printed `unrelatedOrphanSelected: true` and failed with `Expected to not contain: 81592; Received: [81592]`. stopMarkedProcesses will send SIGTERM and potentially SIGKILL to that selected process, allowing one invocation to terminate unrelated work.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts a detached macOS platform process in the same checkout or captured scratch directory and exits. Invocation cleanup selects and kills that unrelated orphan.

gold.summary: Pre-aborted shutdown with failed leader inspection references timer cleanup before initialization and never settles.

findings.title: Working directory and birth time do not establish process ownership
findings.detail: The orphan fallback selects unrelated processes merely because they started during the invocation and share its working directory. Reproduced with an independently launched, detached, empty-environment sleep process. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-SaMTh6/claude-501/review-377.ULtj4q/process-ownership.ts`. Output: `unrelatedProcessSurvived: false (expected true)`. Finishing an ordinary command killed the unrelated process.
findings.failure_scenario: Another run or user launches an orphan with an empty or hidden environment in the same directory while a factory command is running. The factory kills it when its own command finishes.

findings.title: Shutdown is confirmed while detached descendants remain alive
findings.detail: Discovery misses a detached descendant that clears its environment and changes cwd outside the recorded roots before its parent exits. The new shutdown loop then reports success. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-SaMTh6/claude-501/review-377.ULtj4q/process-ownership.ts`. Output: `descendantSurvived: true (expected false)`. The fixture launches the descendant from inside runProcess with env={}, cwd='/', detached=true and stdio='ignore'.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer backgrounds a detached tool with a sanitized environment and a different cwd. That tool continues writing to absolute worktree paths after runProcess returns, racing cleanup.

findings.title: The gate timeout rerun bypasses cleanup recovery
findings.detail: Only the initial checkoutCommitted call receives retryClean. If gates time out, the second call at line 1109 uses the default false. Its clean failure remains a CommandError, so the catch at line 1164 rejects it instead of treating it as a failed implement round. A transient cleanup failure can therefore still fail the whole run after a stuck implementer.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implement round reaches gates; the first cleanup succeeds; gates time out; the clean before the gate rerun fails once; final discard succeeds. The run fails without retrying that clean or advancing to another implement round.

gold.summary: The reader loopback policy cannot match the intended socket access.
An allow-default reader policy weakens the established confinement boundary.

findings.title: Preserve installed Rust toolchain discovery when replacing HOME
findings.detail: Reader commands replace HOME with empty scratch without preserving RUSTUP_HOME. Standard rustup installations consequently lose their default compiler, although gates explicitly preserve RUSTUP_HOME in runConfined. Reproduced with `env HOME="$TMPDIR" rustup show active-toolchain`, which outputs `error: no active toolchain`. Adding `RUSTUP_HOME="$HOME/.rustup"` returns `stable-aarch64-apple-darwin (default)`.
findings.failure_scenario: A Rust repository uses a standard rustup installation with no explicit RUSTUP_HOME environment variable. Its cargo tests pass gates, but the verifier's reader command cannot discover the installed compiler after HOME changes to scratch, blocking verification.

gold.summary: Free-text claim detection still lets model wording steer gate-evidence substitution.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the loopback workaround
findings.detail:
passed() rejects any check containing a skipped file, and applyGateEvidence requires every check to satisfy passed(). Consequently, a successfully executed loopback test cannot supply evidence when an unrelated platform test is skipped. This repository deliberately skips tests when LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, which runConfined sets, so its normal gates cannot supply the intended evidence. Reproduction: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.test.ts". The assertion 'an unrelated platform skip must not invalidate a passing loopback file' failed with:
Expected: "met"
Received: "blocked"
findings.failure_scenario: The confined bun test gate exits zero and records test/loopback.test.ts in passedFiles, while a separate nested-Seatbelt test is skipped. The verifier cannot bind loopback, reports blocked, and the engine still ends verification as needs_human despite passing coverage of the requested test.

findings.title: Ordinary mentions of gates invalidate independent verification
findings.detail:
The sanitizer treats any standalone 'gate' as reliance on factory results, even in independently observed implementation evidence. It also applies a matching notes field to every criterion. Valid met results become blocked and their evidence is erased; inspection criteria cannot recover through command-based gate substitution. Reproduction: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.test.ts". The assertion 'independent code inspection mentioning a gate must remain met' failed with:
Expected: "met"
Received: "blocked"
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier marks an authentication criterion met with evidence 'Inspected src/auth.ts:42: the authentication gate rejects a missing token before calling the handler.' The engine changes it to blocked despite no environmental failure, potentially exhausting verification retries and stopping delivery.

gold.summary: Matching a successful command does not establish the observation required by the criterion.
Targeted Bun evidence can satisfy a criterion without proof that any tests ran.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the fix for confined factory gates
findings.detail: Any skipped test anywhere in the gate suite rejects substitution for every criterion, even when retained coverage proves the requested file passed completely. This repository deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal passing suite cannot resolve the reported loopback verification blocks. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-review.ucgpf7/repro.test.ts"` failed the passing-file/unrelated-skip assertion with `Expected: "met"; Received: "blocked"`.
findings.failure_scenario: The full `bun test` gate passes a local-server CLI test and skips test/sandbox.test.ts cases because LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1. The verifier reports that CLI test blocked by its sandbox. Substitution refuses the passing evidence and the run still ends needs_human.

findings.title: Candidate-controlled output can fabricate authoritative test coverage
findings.detail: The collector treats arbitrary stdout/stderr as trusted runner headers and passing rows. A candidate test can print `test/loopback.test.ts:\n(pass) forged server check` and make the engine substitute a passing verdict for that nonexistent file. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-review.ucgpf7/repro.test.ts"` ran a real Bun decoy test, recorded `passedFiles: ["test/loopback.test.ts", "decoy.test.ts"]`, and failed with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"`.
findings.failure_scenario: A candidate contains only decoy.test.ts, which prints a fabricated passing header for the acceptance test. The broad gate exits successfully, and a sandbox-blocked acceptance criterion is marked met although its required test never existed or ran.

findings.title: Preserve Bun's distinction between substring filters and exact paths
findings.detail: Removing leading `./` makes different Bun commands equivalent, and the matching-command shortcut then accepts them without checking discovered files. Bun treats `test/loopback.test.ts` as a substring filter but `./test/loopback.test.ts` as an exact path. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-review.ucgpf7/repro.test.ts"` confirmed `substring exit 0 exact-path exit 1`, then failed substitution validation with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"`.
findings.failure_scenario: Only other/test/loopback.test.ts exists. The gate `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` passes that file, while the acceptance command `bun test ./test/loopback.test.ts` fails because its exact file is absent. The engine nevertheless marks the blocked acceptance command met.

gold.summary: Manual push reloads mutable clone configuration after its final validation snapshot.
Inherited Git configuration causes validation and push to inspect different settings.
An exact upstream URL requirement rejects supported forks and alternate origin spellings.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land queue push paths
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch receives the requested protection. Both still consume repository-scoped command settings through worktreeGit. A local probe invoking these exports with a planted core.sshCommand produced `delivery: repository command executed = true` and `land: repository command executed = true`. Command: `env -u GIT_SSH_COMMAND -u GIT_SSH bun "$TMPDIR/review-push-probe.ts"`. The planted command only created a marker and exited; no network was used.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants core.sshCommand in repository config. Delivery or land queue publication subsequently invokes that command.

findings.title: Config snapshots do not isolate the final push
findings.detail: The final push still reads repository config and targets origin. A surviving check subprocess can change config after the final snapshot. A local probe using the script's actual validation functions passed validation and snapshot equality, then planted core.sshCommand before the unchanged push invocation. Command: `bash "$TMPDIR/review-race-probe.sh"`; output: `After successful validation and equal snapshots: repository command executed = true`. The new checks leave the underlying vulnerability open.
findings.failure_scenario: An unconfined check leaves a background process that writes command-running config between the last snapshot and Git reading config for push.

findings.title: Allow ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist rejects harmless existing settings, including user.name, user.email, and additional remotes. This prevents otherwise valid repositories from landing. Command: `bash "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.sh"`; a fresh repository passed, but adding only user.name produced `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and exit status 1.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer configures their commit identity locally and invokes land-pr.sh. The script exits before installing dependencies or running checks.

findings.title: Adjust the integration tests' execution budget
findings.detail: `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts` failed the missing and clean final-PR cases at 5000 ms. The isolated command `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'land validates the final PR after CI: (missing|clean)$'` reproduced both timeouts and `Expected: true, Received: false` at line 850. With `--timeout 30000`, both passed in 6406 ms and 6310 ms. The added config subprocesses leave these integration cases beyond their default timeout on this machine.
findings.failure_scenario: The default check runs these cases on a loaded machine; Bun times them out and fails the suite despite their eventual successful behavior.

gold.summary: The loop detector aborts before the threshold call can return evidence of progress.

findings.title: Wait for the threshold call's result before declaring it identical
findings.detail: observe still returns a stop reason before the current result is available. Both harnesses immediately abort and retain stuckReason, so observeResult cannot rescue a progressing sixth call. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { const reason = d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i), i < 5 ? "waiting" : "progress"); assert.equal(reason, null, `call ${i + 1} must not stop when its result changes`); }'. Output: AssertionError: call 6 must not stop when its result changes; actual: 'repeated the same shell call 6 tim
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polling calls return 'waiting'; the sixth would return 'progress'. The harness aborts when the sixth call starts, before learning that it made progress.

findings.title: Compare results in call order rather than completion order
findings.detail: Every completion overwrites results[key], including older calls finishing after newer ones. This makes a subsequent unchanged result look like progress and incorrectly clears the window. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); d.observe("shell", "poll", "1"); d.observeResult("1", "A"); d.observe("shell", "poll", "2"); d.observe("shell", "poll", "3"); d.observeResult("3", "B"); d.observeResult("2", "A"); for (let i = 4; i <= 9; i++) { const reason = d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i), "B"); if (i === 9) assert.equal(reason, "repeated the s
findings.failure_scenario: Calls 1 and 2 return A, call 3 returns B, but completion order is 1, 3, 2. Calls 4 through 9 all return B. Call 4 is incorrectly treated as another change, so six unchanged calls fail to trip the detector.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

findings.title: Out-of-order results can stop calls whose outputs all differ
findings.detail: Only the last call's unresolved result delays detection. If six parallel identical calls complete in reverse order, the sixth call's result immediately triggers a stop before the preceding results can establish progress. Both harnesses abort on that verdict. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as a } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<6;i++) d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); a.equal(d.observeResult("5", "5"), null);' Output: AssertionError: actual 'repeated the same shell call 6 times', expected null. Feeding equivalent real-shaped Claude events reproduces the same failure.
findings.failure_scenario: Six identical calls are issued concurrently, with respective outputs 0 through 5. Call 5 completes first; the detector returns stuck immediately and the harness cancels the invocation before the remaining distinct results arrive.

gold.summary: Increasing panel test deadlines leaves the underlying parallel Git race undiagnosed.
Factory gate environment construction discards the configured test worker override.

findings.title: Preserve the worker override in the factory gate environment
findings.detail: Factory gates use gateEnv(), which calls agentEnv(); agentEnv strips every LIMITLESS_ variable. Consequently this command always selects four workers in factory runs. Verification: `LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=6 bun -e 'import { agentEnv } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; console.log(agentEnv().LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS ?? "missing")'` outputs `missing`. Executing the configured worker expression with that environment resolved to 4.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=2 to reduce contention between simultaneous factory gates; each gate still launches four workers.

findings.title: Supply the requested performance measurements
findings.detail: The change selects four workers but supplies no measurement report. The request explicitly requires comparisons at 4, 6 and 8 workers, serial versus parallel wall/user/system time, the slowest ten files after splitting, and three successful parallel suite runs. Without these results, the chosen default and two-minute file target remain unsubstantiated. I could not obtain meaningful pipeline timings with the installed dependency mismatch.
findings.failure_scenario: The default ships without evidence that it improves throughput or that the split meets the requested per-file duration target.

gold.summary: Unlimited quota still applies utilization reserves to free and metered providers.

findings.title: Honor unlimited quota regardless of billing type
findings.detail: Window bypass is restricted to subscription providers, although configuration accepts unlimited for every billing type. Probe command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {ProviderTracker} from "./src/router/providers.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const t=new ProviderTracker([{id:"work",label:"Work",harness:"fake",billing:"free",quota:"unlimited",maxConcurrent:1}],s,{claudeFiveHour:0.8,claudeSevenDay:0.85,codexFiveHour:0.9,codexWeekly:0.9},{},{},()=>1000000); t.observeWindows("work",{five_hour:{utilization:1,resetsAt:2000000}}); console.log(JSON.stringify({headroom:t.headroom("work"),available:t.isAvailable("work"),reason:t.status("work")?.reason})); s.close();' Obs
findings.failure_scenario: A free or metered provider configured with quota="unlimited" reports a fully utilized window and is excluded from routing despite no CLI rejection.

findings.title: Clear existing window alerts when switching to unlimited
findings.detail: The early return prevents new window alerts but leaves persisted alerts active. An in-memory probe created a 99% five_hour alert with resetsAt:null, reconstructed the tracker with quota="unlimited", called refreshAlerts(), and observed a zero-utilization window. The result still contained the exhausted five_hour alert and the message "Router skips this provider", while headroom was 1. With no reset boundary, this stale alert remains indefinitely.
findings.failure_scenario: A provider has an existing window alert, then the daemon restarts after quota="unlimited" is configured. The dashboard continues showing the old exhaustion alert.

gold.summary: A fixed review-time cutoff excludes worktrees created before the sidecar-writing release actually started.

findings.title: Use installation provenance instead of a fixed release timestamp
findings.detail: The migration equates the sidecar commit timestamp with when every installation upgraded. An installation still running the previous release after that timestamp legitimately creates worktrees without sidecars, but these runs never become eligible for registration. Probe: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501/legacy-cutoff-probe.ts`. It created an old-schema database with a successful prepare after the cutoff and a real linked worktree without a sidecar, then upgraded it. Output: `Old-schema worktree prepared after release cutoff; eligible on upgrade: false` and `Resume git
findings.failure_scenario: An installation runs the pre-#323 release past the hardcoded cutoff, parks a run, and subsequently upgrades. Its intact worktree remains unrecorded and the resumed run fails.

findings.title: Handle legacy local worktrees owned by the source repository
findings.detail: Registration always receives cachePath, and the new validator requires a bare cache. Existing local-run compatibility explicitly supports worktrees owned by the original source repository, whose factory cache may not exist. Probe: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-Xb6sh6/claude-501/legacy-local-probe.ts`. A real source-owned linked worktree produced `Legacy local source-owned worktree: Unsafe worktree Git administration`, caused by ENOENT for the nonexistent factory cache. Passing its actual owner also produced `Using actual owner: Unsafe worktree Git administration`. Existing local compa
findings.failure_scenario: A local run created before factory-owned clones and sidecars is parked and resumed after upgrading. Even with legacy database provenance and intact Git administration, registration fails before the run can continue.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: Compare repository names case-insensitively in check-run URLs
findings.detail: GitHub repository identifiers are case-insensitive, but this exact URL comparison rejects valid jobs when GitHub's canonical casing differs from the configured slug. Classification throws before recording the failure or requesting a rerun, and subsequent polls repeat the error. Probe command: `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-case-review-probe.ts"`. With configured slug `Octocat/Hello-World` and response URL containing `octocat/Hello-World`, observed output was `{"reruns":0,"logs":["GitHub poll of Octocat/Hello-World failed: Error: Incomplete failing job"]}`. Changing only the response URL casing to match the configured slug produced `{"controlReruns":1,...}`. The probe exited 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory repository is configured as `Octocat/Hello-World`, while GitHub returns a timed-out job whose check_run_url uses `octocat/Hello-World`. The eligible job is never rerun or classified.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: A rate-limited rerun remains pending forever
findings.detail: The rerun claim is persisted before the POST, but a rate-limit rejection leaves it as rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections only wait for a newer workflow attempt, which will never exist when GitHub rejected the request. Probe: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probe.test.ts"` returned 429 with Retry-After: 2, then advanced ten minutes of polling. Observed: `outcome: "rerun_requested"`, `reruns 1 needs_fix 0`; the actionable-outcome assertion failed (Expected true, Received false). Existing tests simulate a later rerun even after rejection, masking this case.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub rejects the rerun POST with HTTP 429 or a secondary rate-limit response; no workflow attempt starts, and no user manually reruns it.

findings.title: Compare repository names case-insensitively in returned job URLs
findings.detail: The job check_run_url comparison uses the configured repository casing exactly. GitHub repository names are case-insensitive, and returned URLs can use canonical casing. This rejects valid job evidence indefinitely, preventing both classification and reruns. The rerun reconciliation prefix at line 265 has the same issue. gold.summary: The loop detector aborts before the threshold call can return evidence of progress.

findings.title: The sixth call is stopped before its changed result can arrive
findings.detail: observe() returns a loop reason immediately, and both harnesses immediately abort and latch stuckReason. A subsequent changed result cannot undo that decision. Exact failing command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=1;i<=6;i++){const r=d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`); d.observeResult(`${i}`,i<6?"waiting":"progress"); if(i===6){console.log(r); if(r) throw Error("progress was stopped");}}' Output: repeated the same shell call 6 times; error: progress was stopped (exit 1).
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'; the sixth identical poll returns 'progress'. Both harnesses stop at the sixth tool_call before processing its result.

findings.title: Late results overwrite the result of a newer identical call
findings.detail: The results map tracks completion order instead of call order. An older completion overwrites the newer call's hash, causing a subsequent unchanged result to be treated as progress and clearing valid occurrences. Exact failing command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); d.observe("shell","poll","1"); d.observe("shell","poll","2"); d.observeResult("2","B"); d.observeResult("1","A"); let r; for(let i=3;i<=8;i++){r=d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`); d.observeResult(`${i}`,"B");} console.log(r); if(!r) throw Error("six unchanged results did not stop");' Output: null; error: six unchanged results did not stop (exit 1).
findings.failure_scenario: Identical calls 1 and 2 complete in reverse order with A and B respectively. Calls 3 through 8 all return B. Call 3 incorrectly resets the count because call 1's late A replaced call 2's B, so six unchanged calls do not trip detection.

findings.title: The threshold call is stopped before its changed result arrives
findings.detail: observe() returns the loop reason immediately, and both harnesses irreversibly abort before observeResult() can recognize progress. Direct reproduction: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<6;i++){const r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),i===5?"progress":"waiting"); if(i===5 && r) throw Error(r)}'. Output: error: repeated the same shell call 6 times.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polling calls return 'waiting'; the sixth returns 'progress'. Both harnesses stop the agent on the sixth call before inspecting its changed output.

findings.title: Late results overwrite the baseline of newer identical calls
findings.detail: The results map records completion order rather than call order. An older result arriving late replaces the newer baseline, so the next unchanged result incorrectly clears the window as progress. Direct reproduction: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); const c=(i:number)=>d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); c(1); d.observeResult("1","A"); c(2); c(3); d.observeResult("3","B"); d.observeResult("2","A"); for(let i=4;i<=9;i++){const r=c(i); d.observeResult(String(i),"B"); if(i===9 && !r) throw Error("missed loop at call 9");}'. Output: error: missed loop at call 9.
findings.failure_scenario: Calls 1 and 2 produce A, but call 2 finishes after call 3 produces B. Calls 4–9 all produce B. Call 4 is incorrectly treated as changed, so the six unchanged calls after call 3 fail to trip the detector.

gold.summary: Unlimited quota still applies utilization reserves to free and metered providers.

findings.title: Unlimited quota only bypasses reserves for subscription billing; metered/free unlimited providers are still gated by windows
findings.detail: headroom() skips window utilization only when `p.def.billing === "subscription" && p.def.quota === "unlimited"`. Windows are recorded whatever the billing is (observeWindows is called from context.ts, concierge.ts and the evals runner). reserveFor() applies the claude/codex CLI reserves by kind.
